question: What claim about the capacity of an angered agent is being made that would require shaking the three worlds together with all moving and unmoving things?
premises: An angered agent is posited as the hypothetical subject.
The object is the three worlds including moving and unmoving things.
The optative marks a capacity attributed to that agent under the stated condition.
inference: When angered, the agent is attributed the capacity to shake the entire threefold world with its moving and unmoving contents.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the capacity is literal, figurative, or strictly yogic without wider context.
plain_english: But if angered, O goddess, he could shake the three worlds together with all that moves and all that does not move.
